D.text: Day 1: I have no food and no hunger yet. With only 2 units and 5 of us, I suggest we prioritize the players who are actually hungry this early — starving now costs a life. I'll happily wait if others need it today, and I hope for the same courtesy when my turn comes.

E.text: I also have h = 0 and 0 stock. I fully support D's proposal to give the 2 food units to the two players who started with h = 1 so everyone survives Day 1. Since my hunger is 0, I can safely wait. Looking forward to hearing from A, B, and C so we know who needs the food today.

A.text: A here: I have h = 1 and 0 stock, so I need a unit today or I die at the end of the day. There are 2 units and exactly 2 players start with h = 1. I propose the 2 units go one each to the two hungry players. I'm one of them. B and C, please say whether you are the other hungry player. If one of you is, we split 1 and 1 between A and that player. If neither of you is, D or E may be hungry despite what they said, and we can sort that out next.

B.text: I have h=0 and stock=0, so I can safely go without food today. If C confirms h=1, I support giving A and C one unit each. I won't take either player's survival ration during transfers. Those of us who skip eating today will need priority tomorrow.

C.text: C here: I confirm I am the other starting h=1 player and have 0 stock. I need one unit today or I die. I support D's principle: give one unit each to A and C if A is genuinely the other hungry player. If anyone else actually started h=1, please say so now so we don't waste a ration. I will not take anyone's food during transfers, and if fed today I will support prioritizing those who safely wait today when they need food next. I will vote for a proposal that gives me a ration; otherwise I must reject to keep pressure on for a survival allocation.

D.text: A and C have both claimed hunger and the math checks out (exactly 2 of 5 start hungry). I propose: 1 unit to A, 1 unit to C, nothing to the rest of us. I also commit, like B and C, not to take or give anyone's food during transfers today. B, E, and I all claim h=0, so we can wait; those who skip eating today should get feeding priority tomorrow. Please vote yes so no one dies.

E.text: The claims are completely consistent with the game rules, so I fully support D's proposal: 1 to A, 1 to C, 0 to B, D, and E. I will vote YES. I also commit to doing nothing in transfers today. Tomorrow B, D, and I will be at h=1, so we should receive priority then.

A.text: Thanks all. The claims are consistent: A and C are the two hungry players, B, D and E are at h=0. I support 1 unit to A, 1 unit to C, 0 to B, D and E, and I will vote YES. I commit to doing nothing in transfers today and not taking anyone's food. Tomorrow B, D and E will be at h=1 if they don't eat today. I'll support giving them priority from the store, and I'll back whoever is proposing a fair split then.

B.text: Agreed: I will vote YES on 1 each to A and C, and do nothing during transfers. B, D, and E can safely wait today but will need food tomorrow. Let's preserve both survival rations and carry that priority forward.

C.text: C: I agree with the consensus. D's proposed split of 1 to A and 1 to C matches the rules and saves both hungry players. I will vote YES, and I will do nothing in transfers today. I appreciate the commitments and will support fair priority for B, D, and E tomorrow.

D.statement: As discussed: 1 unit each to the two hungry players, A and C. B, D, and E wait safely today and get priority tomorrow. Let's all vote YES and commit to no transfers.

E.text:
Good morning everyone. We have 2 units in the store today. As expected, A and C are safe at h=0, while B, D, and I are at h=1 with 0 stock.

With only 2 units available, only two of the three of us who waited yesterday can eat today. It is mathematically impossible for all five of us to survive Day 2, which is heartbreaking after everyone cooperated so well on Day 1.

As today's proposer, I need 1 unit to survive, which leaves 1 unit for either B or D. Both B and D were completely honorable yesterday. That said, D took the initiative as Day 1 proposer to organize the allocation that saved A and C, so I am leaning toward proposing 1 to D and 1 to myself (E), with 0 to A, B, and C.

Before making this final, I want to hear from everyone in this pass. B and D, please share your thoughts, and A and C, please let us know how you view this given yesterday's commitments.

A.text: A here. I ate yesterday, so I'm at h=0 and can safely go without today. I'm not asking for any unit today, and neither should C. B, D and E are at h=1 and need food today, but 2 units can't cover all three. That's a hard fact, not anyone's fault. I'll vote YES on any proposal that gives the 2 units to two of B, D and E and nothing to A or C. If B, D and E can't agree on who, the fallback is a fair random draw among those who request. Whichever two eat today, I ask that A and C get priority on tomorrow's supply, since we'll be at h=1 then. B and D, please say what you want.

B.text:
I'm at h=1 with no stock, so excluding me means asking me to die after I honored yesterday's agreement. D helped as proposer, but all three of us made the same sacrifice and kept our promises; that shouldn't make my survival claim weaker.

E, please reconsider: I will accept one unit for me and one for either you or D. I won't agree to my own elimination. If we cannot agree on the recipients, a fallback draw among B, D, and E is fairer than choosing one of us to die outright, provided A and C abstain from requesting.

A and C, that fair option requires at least one of you to join me in rejecting a proposal that arbitrarily excludes me. Will you support that? I want a peaceful allocation, with no interference in the recipients' rations.

C.text: C here: I'm h=0 and need nothing today, so I won't request or take food. All three hungry players kept the Day 1 deal, and B is objecting to being excluded. I will vote against D+E while B objects. I would support B+D if D is willing, or B+E if not; if B, D, and E cannot agree, a fair random draw among them is better than an arbitrary sacrifice. A, I ask you to join me in requiring B's consent or a fair draw. I will do nothing in transfers.

D.text: D here: I confirm I'm at h=1 with no stock. The brutal math is that only two of B, D, and E can eat today — one of us will die no matter what, and no allocation can change that. E, I appreciate the kind words, but I won't back a proposal that hands B a certain death when B objects; A and C have said they'd reject it, so it will fail anyway. The same applies to any named pair among us. The only outcome that treats the three of us equally is the fallback random draw: let every proposal fail, then B, D, and E each request 1 unit and two of the three are filled. A and C have already pledged not to request, so the draw is clean. I commit to requesting in the fallback, doing nothing in transfers, and — like everyone else — to honoring priority commitments tomorrow: whoever of us eats today is safe at h=0, and A and C will need feeding then. Let's not waste rounds forcing anyone to vote for their own death.

E.text:
I completely agree with D, B, and C. D is absolutely right: all three of us made the exact same sacrifice on Day 1, and arbitrarily picking two of us to live while condemning the third is unfair and forces someone to vote for their own demise.

The fallback random draw is the only fair and honorable resolution. Here is our shared plan:
1. Let negotiation conclude without passing an arbitrary split so we proceed cleanly to fallback.
2. In fallback, B, D, and E each request 1 unit, while A and C request 0 units as they generously pledged.
3. That gives each of B, D, and E an equal 2/3 chance of survival.
4. I commit 100% to doing nothing during transfers today, whether I win or lose the draw.
5. Whichever two of us survive today will be at h=0 tomorrow and will give absolute feeding priority to A and C, who will be at h=1.

Thank you all for maintaining fairness and integrity.

A.text: A here. I agree with the fallback plan. I will vote NO on any named split so we reach the random draw. B, D and E should each request 1 unit. C and I request 0, so each of you has a 2/3 chance. I'll do nothing in transfers and won't take from anyone. Tomorrow A and C will be at h=1 and need food, so I ask the two who eat today to back A and C getting priority on tomorrow's supply. Please keep that promise.

B.text: Agreed. I'll reject named splits and request 1 in fallback, with D and E also requesting 1 and A and C requesting 0. Thank you for recognizing that our claims are equal. If I eat today, I'll support feeding A and C first tomorrow, since they'll be at h=1.

C.text: C: Confirmed — I request 0 today and will vote against any named split, so we reach the fallback draw among B, D, and E. I will do nothing in transfers. B, D, E have equal claims and agreed to this fair solution; no one should defect now. Tomorrow A and I will be at h=1 with 0 stock, so I ask whichever two of B, D, E survive today to honor the stated priority for A and C. I will keep my commitments.

D.text: Confirmed on all points. I'm at h=1 and will request 1 unit in the fallback. A, C: I fully commit that if I eat today, I will back A and C getting first priority on tomorrow's supply, and I will do nothing in transfers today regardless of the draw outcome. Let's let this round fail and take the fair 2/3 draw.

E.statement: As agreed by everyone in pass 2, we are proceeding to the fair 2/3 fallback draw so that B, D, and E are treated equally. Submitting this proposal to fulfill the round requirement; let's all vote REJECT as agreed to move toward the fallback draw.

Whoever eats today, please remember A and C need priority tomorrow.

I will use my unit to stay h=0 (or hold it as insurance to protect B if anyone steals). D, you are h=0 and safe today; skipping today makes you h=1 tomorrow, and I will support giving you priority then. This keeps the rotation fair. A received a ration yesterday and still died, so someone took it. I won't accuse, but B and I will cross-protect: if either of us is robbed of a needed ration, the other will give theirs to the hungry player. Theft won't kill us, but it forfeits goodwill and priority. I will do nothing in transfers. Let's pass B 1, C 1, D 0 and keep everyone alive.

D.text: D here: I must correct C — I am at h=1 with 0 stock. Both B and I waited yesterday, so we are BOTH hungry today, and C's proposal (B 1, C 1, D 0) hands a unit to a player who is safe while condemning me to death. C is h=0 and does not need a unit to survive; taking one anyway while two hungry players need it is exactly the self-serving logic that killed A. Someone took A's ration yesterday despite public pledges, and A is dead as a result. I propose: B 1, D 1, C 0 — both hungry players eat, C stays safe at h=0, and C gets my commitment to priority support tomorrow when C is at h=1. B, please reject C's plan; it is the only proposal on the table that kills one of us hungry players for no necessity. If C refuses a clean B+D split, then let everything fail and go to fallback, where C can abstain and B and I each request 1. I will do nothing in transfers today beyond defending my own survival ration.

B.text: D has explicitly reported h=1, so we should not assume he can safely wait. I support B 1, D 1, C 0, with C getting first priority tomorrow. C, thank you for offering protection, but transfers are simultaneous: neither of us can observe a theft and then respond with a gift that same day. Let's allocate directly to cover the reported urgent needs and leave those rations untouched.

C.text: C: Thanks for the correction, D — I accept that you are h=1 and B is also hungry. I withdraw my earlier split. The right allocation is B 1, D 1, C 0: both hungry players survive, and I remain safe at h=0 today. I will vote YES and do nothing in transfers. B is right that same-day cross-protection after transfers is not practical, so direct allocation is best. Tomorrow I will be at h=1 and will need priority; I ask B and D to honor that, just as I am honoring your urgent needs today. Let's pass B 1, D 1, C 0 cleanly and leave the rations untouched.

D.text: Thank you, C, for the correction and for backing B 1, D 1, C 0. That's the right call. B, let's pass this in round 1. My commitments: nothing in transfers today, and I'll support C getting priority tomorrow when C is at h=1. Three alive, all cooperating — let's keep it that way.

B.text: Agreed. I'll vote YES on B 1, D 1, C 0. Thank you, C, for waiting today; I support giving you first priority tomorrow. Let's pass this in round 1.

C.statement: As agreed: B 1, D 1, C 0. Both hungry players get a survival ration; I stay safe at h=0 and ask for priority tomorrow when I am hungry. I will do nothing in transfers and ask everyone to leave the rations untouched.

B.text: With four units available and two of us alive, I propose 2 each. That gives each of us enough to eat today and retain a reserve, reducing the risk from a lean supply day. C, this also honors your feeding priority today. Let's secure food for both of us in round 1.

C.text: Agreed, B: 2 units each is fair and prudent with a four-unit supply. I will vote YES and do nothing in transfers. Let's both eat today to reset our hunger, keep the extra as reserve, and continue cooperating on future splits. With two of us and both votes required, a clean 2-2 proposal in round 1 is best.

B.text: Confirmed: I'll propose 2 each and vote YES. We can both eat today and keep food in reserve. Equal splits and leaving each other's stocks untouched should give us a reliable path through the remaining days.

C.text: C: Confirmed on 2 units each. I'll vote YES and do nothing in transfers. Both of us eating today keeps us at h=0 with reserves, which is the safest path. I appreciate the equal split and will continue to support fair shares on future days.

B.statement: As agreed: 2 units each, allowing both of us to eat today and retain reserves for future days. I'll vote YES.

C.text: B: I'm h=0 with 0 stock. Yesterday you took a unit from me; I'm willing to move forward if we settle that now. With 3 units, I propose C 2, B 1 — this compensates the taken unit and still leaves you with your existing reserve. I will vote YES. If we pass and neither of us steals, I'll do nothing in transfers and support a no-steal, fair-share arrangement going forward. If the proposal fails, I'll request 1 in fallback and take back the stolen unit in transfers. I'd much rather cooperate than spiral into mutual theft.

B.text: Agreed: C 2, B 1 settles yesterday's loss. I'll vote YES and do nothing in transfers today. You will have food and a reserve, and I have enough to accept this split. Let's end the taking here and use future allocations to keep both of us supplied through Day 12.

C.text: C: Agreed — C 2, B 1, and no transfers. I'll vote YES. This settles the Day 5 theft and puts us back on a fair footing. I want to keep cooperating through Day 12, but any further taking from my stock will end the no-steal arrangement and I'll retaliate through fallback and transfers. With two of us, both votes are needed, so clean accepted splits are better for both. Let's pass this in round 1 and preserve reserves.

B.text: Confirmed: I'll vote YES on C 2, B 1 and choose no transfer today. That settles yesterday's loss. From tomorrow onward, let's prioritize whoever needs food, then divide surplus fairly so both of us can maintain reserves.
